mechanical.package: DFN-6 (MAY), 2x2x0.9 mm; also offered as SOT-23-3, SOT-89-3 and TO-92-3

length_mm.conditions: 6-Lead DFN (2x2x0.9 mm) as named in the packaging section; the toleranced outline drawing pages use an encoded font and were not text-extractable

width_mm.conditions: 6-Lead DFN (2x2x0.9 mm) as named in the packaging section; the toleranced outline drawing pages use an encoded font and were not text-extractable

height_mm.conditions: 6-Lead DFN (2x2x0.9 mm) as named in the packaging section

v_in_min.conditions: input operating voltage. Note 1: minimum VIN must satisfy BOTH VIN >= 2.3 V AND VIN >= VR + 3.0% + VDROPOUT, so the practical floor rises with the programmed output.

v_in_max.conditions: input operating voltage; absolute maximum VDD is 6.5 V

i_quiescent.conditions: IL = 0 mA, VIN = VR + 1 V, TA = +25 C, COUT = CIN = 1 uF X7R; 4 uA max over TJ = -40 C to +125 C

i_max.conditions: maximum output current for VR >= 2.5 V (200 mA for VR < 2.5 V). This is a maximum AVERAGE continuous rating; higher pulsed loads are permitted so long as the average stays under it. Typical internal current limit is 550 mA at TA = +25 C, and short-circuit current is 408 mA typ.

theta_ja.conditions: 2x2 DFN-6 with exposed thermal pad, EIA/JEDEC JESD51-7, FR-4 4-layer board

variables.v_in_max: Maximum input voltage seen at VIN -- from the mission operating point (battery top-of-charge or upstream rail)
variables.v_out_min: Minimum output voltage of the LDO, i.e. the programmed VR at its low tolerance corner. The datasheet worked example uses 0.97 * VR.
variables.i_out_max: Maximum load current drawn by the downstream circuit -- from the mission operating point. Dissipation from the 1.6 uA quiescent current is explicitly called insignificant.

t_junction_max.conditions: maximum continuous operating junction temperature TJ; absolute maximum junction temperature is 150 C, and thermal shutdown protection trips at 140 C typ (page 4)

conducted.reason: Ripple on the input rail passed straight through to the regulated output. 100 Hz sits inside the ECG signal band, and this is the only PSRR figure specified numerically -- a neighbouring switcher's fundamental in the MHz will be rejected far less well than this number suggests.

psrr_db.conditions: f = 100 Hz, COUT = 1 uF, IL = 50 mA, VIN AC = 100 mV pk-pk, CIN = 0 uF, VR = 1.2 V

design_notes.note: Output noise is 3 uV/sqrt(Hz) at 1 kHz with IL = 100 mA and COUT = 1 uF. Unlike the TPS7A02 this is a spot noise density, not an integrated figure, so a wideband noise budget for a downstream analog front end has to be built from it rather than read off directly.

Package choice moves theta_JA by more than 2x across the orderable options (91 C/W for the 2x2 DFN-6 versus 212 C/W for the SOT-23) on the SAME JESD51-7 4-layer board. At 218 mW the worked example gives a 46.2 C junction rise in SOT-23; the same dissipation in the DFN gives roughly half that. Any thermal claim must name the package.

Microchip warns that the tabulated theta_JA comes from the JESD51-7 standard board and that actual thermal resistance in an application varies with copper area and thickness, referring the designer to AN792 for how much power a SOT-23 can really dissipate. The table value is a comparison figure, not a board prediction.

The 250 mA rating is a maximum average continuous rating, not a peak. Pulsed loads above it are allowed and the internal current limit (550 mA typ) protects the part, so a duty-cycled radio or sensor burst is a legitimate load -- but average dissipation, and therefore the thermal emission, must be computed on the average current.

provenance.notes: No emissions.conducted entry: this is a CMOS linear LDO with a pass device, so there is no switch node and none of the schema's conducted mechanisms apply. Its own output noise is a spot density (3 uV/sqrt(Hz) at 1 kHz) and is recorded as a design note rather than forced into the ripple field. NOTE a documented internal inconsistency: the Thermal Package Resistance table (page 4) gives SOT-23 theta_JA = 212 C/W, while the narrative on page 14 says the SOT-23 junction-to-ambient resistance 'is estimated at 230 C/W'. The table value (212) was recorded, and the worked example on page 15 also uses 212. Package body dimensions come from the '6-Lead DFN (2x2x0.9 mm)' label in section 7.1 because the toleranced package outline drawings (pages 18-24) are rendered with an encoded font that pdftotext returns as mojibake -- no toleranced dimension was readable, so none was invented. mechanical.* describes the DFN-6 because it is the only option with an exposed thermal pad and the only one whose body size the document states in plain text; all four package theta_JA values are kept in the array. Page numbers are PDF page numbers, which coincide with the printed 'DS20001826E-page N' numbers.
